lesson_title: You Are a Slow Fire: Respiration Is Not Breathing
hook_text: Every cell in your body is burning right now, with no flames. And no, that is not what breathing means.
clip_script: A braai needs fuel and oxygen, and gives off carbon dioxide, water and heat. Now listen: glucose plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water plus energy. Same thing. That is respiration, and it is happening in every one of your cells right now, in tiny structures called mitochondria, with no flames, at 37 degrees. It is why you are warm. Here is the trap everyone falls into. Breathing is not respiration. Breathing is the delivery truck: lungs pull in air, blood carries oxygen to the cells and carts the carbon dioxide back. Respiration is the fire inside the cell. A fish respires with no lungs. A tree respires with no lungs and no blood, day and night, every cell. Want proof? Sprouting seeds in a sealed jar turn clear limewater milky, because living cells make carbon dioxide. Boiled seeds leave it clear. Fuel plus oxygen, energy out. You are a slow fire.
visual_style: A braai flame morphs into a cell with glowing mitochondria; a delivery truck labelled Breathing drives oxygen to the cell and carbon dioxide away; a jar of seeds beside a tube of limewater clouds over.
pacing: Braai hook, quick equation, a sharp brake on the breathing myth, limewater proof, one-line landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set the two equations side by side.
